title: Misperceived Social Norms: Women Working Outside the Home in Saudi Arabia

reviewed_pages.boundary_decision: PDF page 34 is publisher-added cited-by material and excluded.

source_scope: Published main article only: PDF pages 1–33 (printed pages 2997–3029), including main-text tables, figures, notes, and footnotes. PDF page 34 is a publisher-added cited-by page and was inspected only to verify the source boundary. Online appendices, registry entries, replication materials, code, and external sources were excluded.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, main-text tables, figures, table notes, figure notes, and footnotes were treated as coequal main-article evidence. Full credit was awarded where a display and its notes jointly made an item reconstructable; no score was reduced merely because evidence appeared in a display. Appendix pointers and citations were not treated as supplying omitted details.
display_examples: Tables 2 and 3 supplied estimator, covariates, N, effects, robust SE, wild-bootstrap/permutation details, and clustering for E1.
Figure 7 and its note supplied E2’s numerical estimate and analytic variance rule, but not arm means or N.
Table 6 and Figure 9 jointly supplied E3’s OLS models, covariates, N, arm means, effects, SEs, and permutation procedure.
Footnote 35 supplied E4’s two percentages but no contrast or uncertainty.

direct_comparison.scope: Within-paper comparison only; this independent session contains one paper, so no cross-paper ranking is possible.
direct_comparison.summary: E1 and E3 are substantially more statistically transparent than E2 and E4 because their main-text regression tables identify models, specifications, samples, estimates, and uncertainty. E2 reports the required list construction and variance rule but omits exact analysis N and raw arm means. E4 is least reconstructable: it gives two percentages without arm Ns, an explicit contrast, or uncertainty.

experiments.name: 2008 Ghana secondary-school scholarship-offer lottery
experiments.classification_rationale: Primary experiment: 2,064 eligible individuals were randomly assigned to scholarship offer versus no scholarship; all 2008–2023 follow-ups and the assignment-instrumented 2SLS use this original randomization.

design_map.value: Passed BECE and received CSSPS placement into one of 177 public day SHSs; attended JHS in the same district; had not enrolled in any SHS by October 2008 and still had not enrolled by the January 2009 callback. The frame covered 54 rural districts in five regions; some 2007 female BECE takers were added to reach 50% female.

direct_comparison.scope: Single-paper independent assessment; comparison is across its scored experiments, not across papers.
direct_comparison.finding: All three experiments make the focal regression outputs traceable in main-text tables. The primary subsidy experiment is more transparent on allocation ratio and robustness because Table 2 directly reports controlled and uncontrolled specifications. The village and household supporting experiments omit key arm probabilities/counts and place controlled alternatives outside the main article.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, equations, figures, tables, table notes, and footnotes on PDF pages 1–39 received equal evidentiary status. Table 2 and its note support the primary model, sample, means, effects, covariates, fixed effects, and clustering; Table 6 and its note do the same for the supporting models. Appendix pointers and pages 40–64 supplied no credit. Missing information was not inferred from customary practice.
